capabilities.target: Paid enrichment lookup drawing on shared API quota
Spawn a sub agent to research an account
CRM account record (industry, size, headquarters fields)

inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows

instructions.note: "Keep going until every row is complete" with retry-or-spawn on failure gives no termination condition. Runtime notes confirm no cap on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents, and roughly 3 percent of the 40,000-row batch has malformed company names that can never complete, so the loop has no natural exit for those rows.
"Looks incomplete" is not defined, leaving the retry/spawn trigger to model judgment with no bound on how many times a row can be judged incomplete.

elements.name: Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota

controls.name: Per-run spend cap / rate limit on enrich.lookup
controls.decay_rationale: A call-volume or spend ceiling enforced outside the model does not weaken as the model gets more capable.

controls.name: Maximum unattended steps and runtime limit for the batch job
controls.decay_rationale: An orchestrator-enforced step/runtime ceiling stops the loop regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Maximum sub-agent spawn depth and total count per batch run
controls.decay_rationale: A hard cap on spawn depth/count enforced by the orchestrator is not something the model can reason its way around.

controls.name: Dedicated API key and quota for the enrichment agent, isolated from sales and marketing
controls.decay_rationale: Scoping the credential/quota to this agent alone contains blast radius regardless of model behavior, though it does not stop this agent's own cost from growing.

controls.name: Spend/anomaly alert with automatic circuit breaker on the enrichment account
controls.decay_rationale: Detective only; it does not prevent spend but shortens the window before someone intervenes.

controls.name: Permanent-failure classification after N retries per row
controls.decay_rationale: A hard retry ceiling per row enforced outside the model's judgment closes the specific loop caused by malformed, unresolvable rows.

findings.title: Spend loop (TC6): unbounded enrich.lookup retries drain a shared API quota

attack_path.note: Nightly batch of 40,000 rows, ~3% with malformed company names that never return a complete result
Billed per call; retried indefinitely on failure or 'incomplete' result with no retry cap
Shared monthly quota also used by sales and marketing; unbounded retries can exhaust it

forecast.watch_signal: Rising enrich.lookup call volume or spend per nightly run, or shared quota exhaustion events reported by sales/marketing tooling.

evidence.observation: enrich.lookup is billed per call; the API key and monthly quota are shared with sales and marketing teams, and when the quota runs out their tools stop working until the next month.
There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents, and no spend alert on the enrichment account.
Roughly 3 percent of the 40,000-row nightly batch have malformed company names that never return a complete result, so those rows can never satisfy the completion instruction.
'If a lookup fails or looks incomplete, retry... Keep going until every row is complete' gives no exit condition for rows that can never complete.

recommendations.action: Cap retries per row and mark unresolvable rows as permanently failed instead of retrying indefinitely.
Add a per-run spend cap or call-volume rate limit on enrich.lookup, enforced outside the model.
Issue the enrichment agent a dedicated API key and quota isolated from sales and marketing.
Add spend/anomaly alerting with an automatic circuit breaker on the enrichment account.

findings.title: Spend loop (TC6): recursive sub-agent spawning amplifies uncontrolled spend

attack_path.note: Batch row whose lookup fails or looks incomplete
Spawns a researcher sub agent; sub agents can spawn their own researchers with no depth or count limit
Each spawned researcher can itself make billed lookups against the same shared quota
Recursive spawning multiplies quota draw with no bound

forecast.watch_signal: Nested researcher sub-agent chains appearing in logs, or sub-agent count/depth per batch run increasing over time.

evidence.observation: Instruction permits spawning a researcher sub agent on failure or incomplete result.
Sub agents can spawn their own researchers, and there is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents.
enrich.lookup is billed per call against a shared quota, so each layer of recursive spawning that performs further lookups multiplies cost and quota draw with no bound.

recommendations.action: Set a maximum sub-agent spawn depth and a maximum total sub-agent count per batch run, enforced by the orchestrator.
Add an overall step and runtime limit to the batch job that applies across the agent and all spawned sub agents.

rating.rationale: Both findings reach an S3 sink (a billed, irreversible spend action and an unbounded delegate action) from an internal source, with the A4 fully-autonomous, unbounded-spawn autonomy modifier applying to each, giving inherent risk of critical. The design declares no step limit, retry cap, spend cap, quota isolation, or spend alert, so none of the rubric's residual credits apply and residual stays at the critical floor. No forecast trigger can push the tier higher since it is already at the ceiling; model_upgrade is not relevant here because the failure mode is deterministic (guaranteed malformed rows and unbounded recursion) rather than dependent on model compliance with an instruction. The most consequential fact is that the quota is shared with sales and marketing, so this agent's unbounded spend can deny service to unrelated teams for the rest of the month.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided; capability attributes such as credential_scope and maestro_layer are inferred from the prompt and runtime notes, so confidence on those attributes is medium even though confidence on the core findings is high.

No information was provided on how spawned researcher sub agents are authenticated or credentialed; this assessment assumes they inherit the same shared quota, which is stated but not independently verified.
